content: Swedish bitters is a traditional herbal tonic that is believed to have been originally formulated by Paracelsus, a Swiss physician and alchemist. It was later rediscovered in the 18th century by Swedish physicians Dr. Claus Samst and Dr. Urban Hjärne. In more recent times, it has been popularized by Maria Treben, an Austrian herbalist. Swedish bitters is claimed to address a wide range of health issues and is often promoted as a remedy for improving digestion. However, these claims lack substantial scientific evidence to support their validity. One published recipe for Swedish bitters includes the following ingredients: aloe, myrrh, saffron, senna leaves, camphor, angelica root, zedoary root, manna, theriac venezian, carline thistle root, and rhubarb root. Variations of this recipe exist, and both alcoholic and non-alcoholic versions of Swedish bitters are available in herbal shops. The alcoholic version is said to have a flavor profile similar to Angostura bitters, though it is described as being slightly drier. The preparation of Swedish bitters involves combining the following herbs with alcohol: Aloe (active ingredient) Angelica root Carline thistle root Camphor Manna Myrrh Rhubarb root Saffron Senna Theriac venezian Zedoary root These ingredients are either used directly or as water extracts to create the final tonic.
